title: ai-for-rstudio
text:
This project explores and demonstrates different uses of AI with R and RStudio.
I’m admittedly not an export on AI or its uses with R or coding in general. I’m learning along with you.

title: 02-copilot-complete
text:
Github Copilot was the first “Copilot”, and that name was later absorbed by Microsoft. It is an AI model trained on all the data on Github, and it does come with some controversy.
Github Copilot of free for students who are authenticated through their program. That program evolves along with everything else in AI. On the day I write this in March 2026, Github is changing the structure, but the result is the same.
Read more here about how to connect to you Github account.
Within RStudio, Copilot acts as a code completion tool. One effective way to use it is to descibe what you want to do within your notebook and then activate it.

title: 02-copilot-complete
text:
The process I used
What packages do I need to start with?

# what packages do I need?

library(rvest)
library(tidyverse)

── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
✔ dplyr     1.1.4     ✔ readr     2.1.5
✔ forcats   1.0.0     ✔ stringr   1.6.0
✔ ggplot2   4.0.1     ✔ tibble    3.3.0
✔ lubridate 1.9.4     ✔ tidyr     1.3.1
✔ purrr     1.1.0     
── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
✖ dplyr::filter()         masks stats::filter()
✖ readr::guess_encoding() masks rvest::guess_encoding()
✖ dplyr::lag()            masks stats::lag()
ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors


Scrape the pages.

url <- "https://cfbstats.com/2025/leader/national/team/offense/split01/category09/sort01.html"

page <- read_html(url)

# pull the table of stats
stats_table <- page |> html_element("table") |> html_table()

# and then view it
stats_table


  



I will need to get different years. Write a function that allows me to enter a year into the function to grab those stats.

get_stats <- function(year) {
  url <- glue::glue("https://cfbstats.com/{year}/leader/national/team/offense/split01/category09/sort01.html")
  
  page <- read_html(url)
  
  stats_table <- page |> html_element("table") |> html_table()
  
  return(stats_table)
}

get_stats("2024")

title: 01-troubleshooting
text:
Here I want to show how you can take an error and try to find out what is going on with a basic GenAI chat experience.

library(tidyverse)


read_csv("data-original/hot100_assignment.csv") |> clean_names()



You can try copy/pasting the error into a browser for the AI or Google answer
Error in clean_names(read_csv("data-original/hot100_assignment.csv")) : 
  could not find function "clean_names"



Leo AI Answer





Or you could do similar with ChatGPT, Claude or ChatGPT





label










In this last instance, ChatGPT went on to give some background about what the package does. This is that extra bit that people who use AI as a crutch instead of a tool fail to get the full benefit.
(The crazy thing is it derived the variables from context or a previous chat because I didn’t supply that.)




It might help to say you are using R or Tidyverse and a package you might need.



label


You might even provide the data. There is a package called datapasta that can help you make a reproducible sample of your data. I used datapasta::dpaste to format the tibble below. This is also useful if you are asking for help on a forum like Stack Overflow.
I have the following data in R:

tibble::tribble(
  ~year, ~district, ~name, ~party, ~candvotes,
  "2016", 46, "Dukes", "D", 37457,
  "2016", 46, "Greeley", "G", 2178,
  "2016", 46, "Ludlow", "L", 3445,
  "2016", 46, "Nila", "R", 10209
)

And I want new columns that do the following:

- the name of the winning candidate (highest candvotes value).
- the percentage of the total vote that the winning candidate received
- the name of the second highest candidate (using candvotes)
- the percentage of the total vote that second candidate got
- the difference betwen the two percentages
You can see the full exchange of the above prompt here.
